title: "Wine - Solutions"
output: html_document

### Introduction:

This exercise is a adaptation from the UCI Wine dataset.
The only pupose is to practice deleting data with R.

### Step 1. Import the necessary libraries

```{r step1, message=FALSE}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
```

### Step 2. Import the dataset from this [address](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/wine/wine.data).

### Step 3. Assign it to a variable called wine

```{r}
url <- "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/wine/wine.data"

# the file has no header row: col_names = FALSE keeps the first row as data
wine <- read_csv(url, col_names = FALSE)

head(wine)
```

### Step 4. Delete the first, fourth, seventh, nineth, eleventh, thirteenth and fourteenth columns

```{r}
wine <- wine |> select(-c(1, 4, 7, 9, 11, 13, 14))

head(wine)
```

### Step 5. Assign the columns as below:

The attributes are (donated by Riccardo Leardi, riclea '@' anchem.unige.it):
1) alcohol
2) malic_acid
3) alcalinity_of_ash
4) magnesium
5) flavanoids
6) proanthocyanins
7) hue

```{r}
names(wine) <- c("alcohol", "malic_acid", "alcalinity_of_ash", "magnesium",
                 "flavanoids", "proanthocyanins", "hue")
head(wine)
```

### Step 6. Set the values of the first 3 rows from alcohol as NA

```{r}
wine$alcohol[1:3] <- NA
head(wine)
```

### Step 7. Now set the value of the rows 3 and 4 of magnesium as NA

```{r}
wine$magnesium[3:4] <- NA
head(wine)
```

### Step 8. Fill the value of NA with the number 10 in alcohol and 100 in magnesium

```{r}
wine <- wine |> replace_na(list(alcohol = 10, magnesium = 100))

head(wine)
```

### Step 9. Count the number of missing values

```{r}
colSums(is.na(wine))
```

### Step 10. Create an array of 10 random numbers up until 10

```{r}
random <- sample(1:10, size = 10, replace = TRUE)
random
```

### Step 11. Use random numbers you generated as an index and assign NA value to each of cell.

```{r}
wine$alcohol[random] <- NA
head(wine, 10)
```

### Step 12. How many missing values do we have?

```{r}
colSums(is.na(wine))
```

### Step 13. Delete the rows that contain missing values

```{r}
wine <- wine |> drop_na()
head(wine)
```

### Step 14. Print only the non-null values in alcohol

```{r}
mask <- !is.na(wine$alcohol)
head(mask)
```

```{r}
wine$alcohol[mask]
```

### Step 15. Reset the index, so it starts with 1 again

```{r}
# tibbles are always numbered from 1 to n, so there is nothing to reset.
# With a base data.frame you would use: rownames(wine) <- NULL
head(wine)
```
